Build a Todo app in a single self-contained HTML file. Requirements:
- Add new todos
- Mark todos as complete (strikethrough)
- Delete todos
- Filter: All / Active / Completed
- Persist to localStorage

Deliver only the HTML file with JS, CSS, HTML. Use file name "todo_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html"

{"path": "todo_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html", "edit_description": "Create a complete, self-contained Todo app HTML file (HTML + CSS + JS in one file, no external dependencies).

Functional requirements:
1. Add new todos: an input field and "Add" button; pressing Enter also adds. Ignore empty/whitespace-only input. Clear input after adding.
2. Mark todos as complete: each todo has a checkbox; completed todos get strikethrough text and a dimmed style.
3. Delete todos: each todo has a delete (✕) button that removes it.
4. Filters: three buttons — All / Active / Completed — that filter the visible list. The active filter button is visually highlighted.
5. Persistence: todos (id, text, completed) are saved to localStorage under a key like 'todos' on every change, and loaded on page load. Handle corrupted JSON gracefully (fall back to empty array).

Implementation details:
- Vanilla JS, no libraries. Use DOM APIs, event listeners (avoid inline onclick handlers where practical).
- Escape user text safely (use textContent, not innerHTML, for todo text) to prevent XSS.
- Show an empty-state message when the filtered list is empty.
- Show an item counter (e.g. "3 items left" counting active todos).
- Each todo gets a unique id (Date.now() + random or crypto.randomUUID with fallback).
- Clean modern CSS: centered card layout, system font stack, subtle shadows, hover states, responsive for narrow screens. All styles in a <style> tag in <head>; all JS in a <script> tag at the end of <body>.
- Include proper <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="en">, meta charset and viewport tags, and a <title>Todo App</title>.
- A "Clear completed" button is optional but welcome."}
